A1.justification: Both PDFs describe successive versions of the same downstream dataset-pruning work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial methodological and experimental revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-classification accuracy and timing results, ablations, architecture-transfer experiments and QWen instruction-tuning results, including additional results in Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 reports original DLC/FlexRand classification and timing experiments, MMLU evaluations, masking and sampling ablations, and transfer results, with additional experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: V1 uses layerwise weighted-KNN confidence for images, reciprocal perplexity across dropout subnets for language, and easy-image selection within K-means clusters. V2 replaces these with L1-based weight masking, prototype-based loss integration approximated by Monte Carlo, and FlexRand sampling from adjustable easy/hard intervals (Sections 3.1–3.3). Scoring, subnet construction and selection procedures change substantially.

E1.justification: CXRB10, DTD/Texture and Sketch are retained, while DeepWeeds and FGVCAircraft add visual domains. UltraChat is replaced by Alpaca Cleaned and Dolly & HH-RLHF; MMLU introduces subject-wise question-answer classification evaluation in place of the earlier response-quality evaluation. V1's ImageNet-21K pretraining coverage is also absent from v2's stated ImageNet-1K setup.

E2.justification: V2 adds SSP to the main image comparison while retaining the other named vision baselines. Its LLM comparison retains Random/Ours but drops v1 Table 3's full-data and Small-score controls. CCS and BoundarySet are related-work additions without reported comparison results. The LC bar in v2 Figure 1 matches Least Conf in Table 1, rather than retaining v1's proposed LC as a baseline.

E3.justification: Image validation changes from 25% to 20%, batch size from 64 to 128, weight decay from zero to 1e-5, and a tuned learning rate to fixed 1e-3; the BatchNorm head component is removed. Model and pretraining configurations change, including adding ViTs and larger LLMs. Geometric baselines now undergo full-data fine-tuning. LLM experiments change from one epoch with 10% data to three epochs with 50% data, LoRA and five-shot MMLU. Nine image budget fractions remain, although v2 inconsistently describes ratios as removed versus retained data.

E4.justification: V1's layer-count and cluster-count sensitivity studies are replaced by learning-path-size, L1-versus-random-masking and interval-splitting studies (v2 Figure 6). V2 adds MMD measurements of sampling-induced distribution shifts, masking-versus-optimization loss analyses and qualitative easy/hard image examples (Figures 2–4 and 7). Architecture transfer is retained with revised experiments; v1's LLM convergence analysis is removed.

E5.justification: V1 presents point estimates without explicit repetition counts or uncertainty displays. V2 Table 1 adds ± quantities for accuracy and timing, Figure 5 adds shaded bands, and Figure 6b examines masking variability across ten seeds. Appendix B.1 newly specifies three seeds for EL2N scoring. The main table's uncertainty statistic and repetition count remain undefined; these disclosures do not establish an increase in runs over v1.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and expanded under changed conditions. V1 Table 1 reports RN18 LC accuracy of 56.86% across three datasets; v2 Table 1 reports 57.31% across five and adds ViT results. V1's LLM perplexity/direct-score results are replaced by MMLU results, including Mistral/Alpaca STEM accuracy of 51.74% for Random versus 52.74% for Ours. V2 also reports 29.5 seconds total pruning time against approximately 1,033 seconds for one-shot baselines. These are revised experiments, not controlled cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: V1 Proposition 3.1 and Appendix B's Gaussian-mixture proof connecting weighted-KNN confidence to density are removed, together with the formal diversity criterion. V2 instead defines Learning Path through limiting risk and Learning Complexity as a loss integral, then develops mathematical arguments for optimization and masking paths and their Monte Carlo approximation. This replaces the formal framework rather than relocating the earlier proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion shift from adapted-score consistency and easy/diverse selection to DLC and FlexRand as the central contributions. V2 adds explicit claims about adapting sampling preferences across data regimes and achieving 35× pruning acceleration. V1's claim of stable LLM tuning outperforming full-data training with 10% of instructions is replaced by superiority over random selection across several LLMs.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanation shifts from representation gaps, early-layer generalization and dense-region redundancy to capacity-based hardness, regime-dependent preferences and sampling-induced distribution shift. V2 interprets missing-label pretraining experiments as evidence of robustness and presents score transfer as an accuracy–efficiency tradeoff; v1 emphasized that transfer could improve performance. V2 also explicitly identifies storage and memory costs from retaining masked models.

D1.justification: V2 Appendix B adds dataset sizes and class counts, learning-path stopping information, the interval-splitting search range, and HuggingFace, PEFT and LM-Eval implementation information. Hardware reporting changes from RTX 4090 to L40, alongside revised training recipes. Dataset counts are newly documented rather than established changes to previously stated sample sizes; the FGVCAircraft counts are internally inconsistent. DeepCore/PyTorch usage and the supplementary-code availability statement remain.

R1.justification: The scientific positioning shifts from early-exit and multilevel-confidence ideas toward weight pruning, model-capacity generalization, optimization trajectories and Monte Carlo estimation. Corresponding references such as Han et al., Neyshabur et al. and Caflisch are added. Appendix A retains its taxonomy but adds SSP, CCS and BoundarySet and expands discussion of the already-cited Moderate Coreset. Its changed publication year does not constitute a new cited work.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method explanation and discussion are extensively rewritten. The separate motivation subsection disappears, instruction pruning becomes a method subsection and a dedicated experimental branch, and detailed settings move into an expanded experimental appendix. Appendix B changes from a proof appendix to experimental documentation, with detailed results organized under B.2 rather than Appendix C.

P2.justification: The main document changes from two-column to single-column layout. V2 adds an opening efficiency/accuracy chart, qualitative image pairs, loss-trajectory grids and MMD displays. Main tables separate architecture columns and scoring/total timing, replacing v1's slash-separated model entries; appendix results become separate architecture-specific tables. Accuracy-gap plots are reorganized by dataset and gain uncertainty bands.

improvement.justification: V2 improves empirical assessability through five visual domains, CNN/ViT coverage, three LLMs with a specified five-shot MMLU protocol, and targeted masking and sampling analyses. Uncertainty displays and an explicit memory limitation also strengthen reporting. These gains are tempered by the loss of v1's training-free geometric comparison setting and full-data LLM control, plus undefined uncertainty statistics and inconsistent pruning-ratio descriptions. The evidence supports a limited net quality improvement despite the extensive revision.
